desc: Owns regulated water, gas and electric utilities in the US and renewable power generation, operating from Ontario.

rationale: Regulated utility with a captive customer base and no marketing culture; F1 sponsorship adds little.

name: Antero Resources
desc: Independent natural gas and natural gas liquids producer with operations in Appalachia in West Virginia and Ohio.
markets: Production in West Virginia and Ohio, with some LNG-linked sales; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic gas producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers limited return.

name: ARC Resources
desc: Canadian oil and gas producer focused on the Montney formation in western Canada, producing natural gas, condensate and light oil.
markets: Production in Western Canada with sales across North America and exposure to LNG-linked pricing.
rationale: Canadian B2B producer without consumer brand; F1 would only add client hospitality, so fit is weak.

name: BW LPG
desc: Owns and operates liquefied petroleum gas carriers, with one of the largest very large gas carrier fleets, within BW Group.
markets: Ships carry LPG between the US, Middle East, Asia and Europe for energy traders and producers.
rationale: B2B shipping firm with few consumer touchpoints; F1 hospitality could suit Singapore and Asian client relationships.

name: Hallador Energy
desc: Indiana company that mines coal and owns the Merom coal-fired power plant, selling power and coal in the Midwest.
markets: Operations in Indiana selling coal and electricity to Midwest utilities; no international activity.
rationale: Domestic coal and power producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is unsuitable.
changed: Acquired the Merom power plant in 2022

name: JSW Energy
desc: Indian power producer in the JSW Group with thermal, hydro, wind, solar and battery storage capacity, expanding in renewables.
markets: Generation assets and customers in India; focus on renewable capacity growth; no verified operations abroad.
rationale: Large Indian industrial group brand with growing renewables business; F1 could support India brand building, though the company is mainly B2B.

name: Liberty Energy
desc: Oilfield services company providing hydraulic fracturing, wireline and proppant logistics to oil and gas producers in North America.
markets: Fracturing fleets serve US producers, mostly in shale basins, with some Canadian activity; no wider international operations.
rationale: B2B oilfield service firm with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has little commercial logic.
changed: Renamed from Liberty Oilfield Services to Liberty Energy in 2022

name: National Fuel Gas Company
desc: Diversified energy company with Appalachian gas production, interstate pipelines and storage, and gas utility distribution in New York and Pennsylvania.
markets: Operations in New York, Pennsylvania and Appalachia only; customers are utility ratepayers, shippers and gas buyers.
rationale: Regional gas utility and producer with little marketing culture; F1 offers no clear commercial return.

name: Serica Energy
desc: Independent North Sea oil and gas producer with interests in fields such as Bruce, Keith, Rhum and Triton.
industry: North Sea oil and gas producer
markets: Production confined to the UK North Sea, supplying UK gas and oil buyers.
rationale: B2B North Sea producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship would be hard to justify.

name: Summit Midstream
desc: Owns and operates natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering systems serving producers in several US basins.
markets: Gathering systems in the Rockies, Mid-Con, Permian and Appalachia serving US producers; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B midstream firm with no consumer brand; very weak F1 fit.
changed: Converted from a partnership to a corporation in 2024

name: Hafnia
desc: Operates one of the world's largest fleets of oil product and chemical tankers, with offices in Singapore and Copenhagen.
markets: Tankers carry refined products and chemicals for oil majors and traders on routes across the world.
rationale: B2B shipping firm with few consumer touchpoints; hospitality at Asian and European races could suit charterers.

name: Harbour Energy
desc: Largest UK North Sea independent oil and gas producer, expanded internationally by acquiring Wintershall Dea's upstream business.
markets: Production in the UK North Sea, Norway, Argentina, Mexico and Southeast Asia; oil and gas sold to European and other buyers.
rationale: B2B upstream producer with no consumer brand; the UK base gives some hospitality logic, but F1 fit is weak.
changed: Formed from Chrysaor and Premier Oil in 2021; acquired Wintershall Dea's upstream business in 2024

name: Murphy Oil Corporation
desc: Independent oil and gas exploration company producing from US onshore, Gulf of Mexico and Canadian offshore assets, plus Asia.
industry: oil and gas exploration and production
markets: Production in the US, Canada, Vietnam and Mexico; oil and gas sold to refiners and traders.
rationale: Upstream producer with no consumer brand; F1 would only offer client hospitality, so fit is weak.

name: Oceaneering
desc: Provides engineered services and robotics, including remotely operated vehicles, for offshore energy, defence, aerospace and entertainment customers.
markets: Subsea services for offshore energy clients worldwide; also supplies defence, aerospace and theme-park ride systems.
rationale: Engineering and robotics firm whose technology story suits F1 showcasing, but customers are B2B and brand awareness is low.

name: ONE Gas
desc: Regulated natural gas distribution utility serving over two million customers in Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas.
markets: Regulated gas utility operating only in Oklahoma, Kansas and Texas.
rationale: Regulated local utility with captive customers and no international footprint; F1 offers essentially no return.

name: Par Pacific
desc: Owns refineries in Hawaii, Washington State, Wyoming and Montana and retail fuel stores in Hawaii and the Pacific Northwest.
markets: Refineries and retail stations in the western US and Hawaii; no operations outside the United States.
rationale: Regional refiner and retailer with local brands; F1 offers limited reach for its Hawaii and Rockies customers.

name: ProPetro
desc: Oilfield services company providing hydraulic fracturing, cementing and wireline services to oil and gas producers in the Permian Basin.
markets: Fleets serve Permian Basin producers in West Texas and New Mexico; no international operations.
rationale: B2B service provider with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little return.

name: Sable Offshore
desc: Oil and gas company operating the Santa Ynez Unit offshore Santa Barbara, California, and associated pipelines, with restart plans.
markets: Single asset offshore California selling crude to US refiners; restart faces regulatory and legal challenges.
rationale: Single-asset US producer with regulatory battles and no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is not credible.
changed: Acquired the Santa Ynez Unit from ExxonMobil in 2024

name: Saturn Oil & Gas
desc: Canadian oil producer focused on light oil in Saskatchewan and Alberta, grown through acquisitions including Oxbow and Ridgeback.
markets: Production in Saskatchewan and Alberta sold to Canadian and US buyers; no operations outside Canada.
rationale: Small Canadian producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship would be disproportionate.

name: SSE
desc: British energy company with renewables, electricity networks, thermal power and energy supply businesses serving customers in the UK and Ireland.
markets: Customers in Great Britain and Ireland; wind and hydro projects mainly in the UK and Ireland, with some offshore wind interests elsewhere.
rationale: Consumer energy brand with sustainability positioning and sports sponsorship history; British Grand Prix and net-zero messaging fit.

name: Ovintiv
desc: North American independent oil and natural gas producer with operations in the Permian, Montney and Anadarko basins.
markets: Production in the US and Canada sold to North American buyers; no other regions.
rationale: B2B upstream producer without consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial value.
changed: Renamed from Encana to Ovintiv on moving its domicile to the US in 2020

name: Ras Laffan Petrochemicals
desc: Joint venture developing a large ethane cracker and polyethylene complex at Ras Laffan Industrial City for global export.
markets: Single petrochemical project in Qatar owned by QatarEnergy and Chevron Phillips Chemical, aimed at export markets.
rationale: Industrial project vehicle with no consumer brand; any Qatari motorsport marketing would sit with QatarEnergy instead.

name: VARO Energy
desc: Swiss-based energy group refining and marketing conventional fuels, with storage, retail fuels and bioenergy businesses in Europe.
markets: Refineries, storage and retail in Europe; originally formed by Vitol and Carlyle; mostly B2B with limited consumer brand.
rationale: Mostly B2B fuel supplier with limited consumer brand; F1 could suit European hospitality but fit is only moderate.

name: CK Hutchison Holdings
desc: Hong Kong conglomerate running ports, retail through A.S. Watson, infrastructure, energy and telecommunications businesses across many countries.
markets: Ports, Watsons and Superdrug retail, UK infrastructure and 3 telecoms operations across Europe, Asia and elsewhere.
rationale: Global conglomerate with consumer retail and telecom brands; F1 offers brand reach and hospitality across Europe and Asia.

name: Coterra Energy
desc: Independent oil and gas producer with Marcellus Shale natural gas in Pennsylvania and oil in the Permian Basin and Anadarko.
markets: Production in Pennsylvania, West Texas and Oklahoma sold to US buyers; no international operations.
rationale: Upstream producer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial logic.
changed: Formed in 2021 by merging Cabot Oil & Gas and Cimarex Energy

name: DNO
desc: Norwegian oil and gas operator producing in Iraqi Kurdistan, the North Sea and parts of Africa and the Middle East.
markets: Production in Kurdistan (Tawke), the North Sea after buying Faroe Petroleum, and other Middle East and African assets.
rationale: B2B upstream operator with no consumer brand; F1 fit is weak beyond occasional hospitality.

name: EnLink Midstream
desc: Gathers, processes, transports and fractionates natural gas, NGLs and crude oil in the Permian, Oklahoma, North Texas and Louisiana.
markets: Pipelines and plants in US basins serving producers and customers; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic B2B midstream firm with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship makes little sense.
changed: Remaining units acquired by ONEOK in 2025

name: Petroperu
desc: Peru's state-owned oil company running the Talara refinery, pipelines and fuel distribution, selling fuels to wholesalers and its station network.
markets: Refining and fuel sales across Peru only; no verified activity abroad.
rationale: State oil company with weak finances and a domestic market; F1 sponsorship is unlikely.

name: Antero Midstream
desc: Provides gathering, compression, processing and water services mainly to Antero Resources in the Appalachian Basin.
markets: Assets in West Virginia and Ohio serving Antero Resources and other producers; no international operations.
rationale: Domestic midstream firm tied to one customer with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship has no logic.
changed: Formed in 2019 by merging Antero Midstream Partners and Antero Midstream GP

name: Apraava Energy
desc: Indian power company with wind, solar, thermal and transmission assets, jointly owned by CLP Group and CDPQ.
markets: Generation and transmission assets across India; backed by investors from Hong Kong and Canada.
rationale: Indian power company with mainly B2B customers and little marketing culture; F1 could support investor profile only.
changed: Rebranded from CLP India in 2022

name: Boardwalk Pipelines
desc: Owns about 14,000 miles of natural gas and liquids pipelines and storage linking Gulf Coast producers to Midwest markets.
markets: Pipelines serve utilities, producers and industrial users in the US only; owned by Loews.
rationale: Pipeline subsidiary with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship makes no commercial sense.

name: Chord Energy
desc: Oil and gas producer focused on the Williston Basin of North Dakota, selling crude and gas to US buyers.
markets: Production in North Dakota's Williston Basin; no international operations.
rationale: Upstream producer with no consumer brand and a single-basin domestic footprint; F1 sponsorship offers little commercial return.
changed: Formed by the 2022 merger of Oasis Petroleum and Whiting Petroleum

name: EnQuest
desc: Independent oil and gas producer operating UK North Sea assets such as the Magnus field and the Sullom Voe terminal.
industry: North Sea oil and gas producer
markets: UK North Sea production and terminal operations, plus interests in Malaysia; oil sold to European and Asian buyers.
rationale: B2B North Sea producer with no consumer brand; F1 would be limited to client hospitality.

name: NTPC
desc: India's largest power company, state-controlled, operating thermal, hydro, solar and wind plants and selling electricity to state utilities.
markets: Plants across India selling to state distribution companies; some overseas joint ventures in the region.
rationale: State-controlled generator with captive buyers; F1 offers only national branding value, so fit is weak.

name: NexGen Energy
desc: Canadian uranium developer advancing the Rook I project and Arrow deposit in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin.
markets: Single project in Saskatchewan; pre-revenue with future sales to nuclear utilities, with no producing operations yet.
rationale: Pre-revenue uranium developer with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit beyond investor visibility.
